name: NJ-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Markets price Gottheimer at ~97% to win
Massive financial advantage: $12.8M on hand vs. $8K for the Republican
Incumbent running in a district with a modest Democratic lean
No public polling, so uncertainty stays elevated
model.rationale: Prediction markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket put Gottheimer's win probability near 97%, and his fundraising edge is overwhelming — over $12.7 million on hand against roughly $8,000 for Sean Kirrane. With the incumbent running in a district that leans Democratic, the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the race unexpectedly competitive, or a major outside-spending surge against Gottheimer, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Josh Gottheimer, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a northern New Jersey district that leans slightly Democratic. He enters the general election with a dominant financial position, having raised $4.8 million and holding $12.8 million on hand. Republican Sean Kirrane has raised only about $56,000, leaving him with minimal resources to compete, and no outside spending has materialized on either side.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have listed the race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Both Kalshi and Polymarket put Gottheimer's chances near 97%. The expected margin is a comfortable double-digit Democratic win, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat wide.
